dataset: SGO crash-report trend shifts and the evidence around them
method: Monthly ADS crash counts by incident month are split into straight-line segments (square-root scale, penalised dynamic programming, minimum six months). A break is kept only if the average level or the growth rate changes materially. Evidence lists facts computed from this site's data; coincident public events are context, not proven causes.

evidence: Growth in monthly reports changed from +5 to +32 a month each year. Reports averaged 9 a month in Oct 2022 to Dec 2022 and 37 in Aug 2023 to Oct 2023.
17 cities first appear in the reports during this period, led by Santa Monica, CA, Paradise, NV, Houston, TX, Grand Rapids, MN. By Oct 2023 they account for 12% of monthly reports.
First reports from GA, WA.
Monthly reports rose most at Cruise (+18), Waymo (+10); fell at Zoox (-1). Waymo is 38% of reports at the end of the period.
Highway or freeway crashes were 7.5% of reports before the period and 3.6% at its end.
New vehicle platforms in the reports: Nissan LEAF (3).
Reporting rules changed during this period: NHTSA's second amended SGO took effect in May 2023, so counts before and after are not strictly comparable.

coincident_events.title: California suspends Cruise driverless permits
coincident_events.text: On Oct. 24, 2023 the California DMV suspended Cruise's deployment and driverless testing permits after a pedestrian was dragged by a Cruise vehicle. Cruise paused its San Francisco driverless operations, and no Cruise reports appear in this dataset after October 2023.
